advances: Actual depth on the full sampled set, including pure-base normals and all middle tip-axis points. Baseline uniqueness and nearby global maximality have different scopes.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Since $0\in K_p$, concavity of $r^0$ and convexity of $K_p$ imply convexity of the radial body; continuity and positive radii on the compact full-dimensional base give compactness and full dimension. Its sampled sections have exactly the given radii. At $Y$, any closed containing halfspace can be tightened to pass through the point. In each opposite-base pair the radii agree and continuous thresholds are opposite. Apply the bipyramid paired-menu theorem and the central ordinary bound to get mass at least $Q_0$ when the continuous normal is nonzero. A pure-base cap through $Y$ contains at least one entire fiber of each pair and the whole middle fiber, so its mass is at least $M_0/2>Q_0$. Canonical cylinders have exactly $Q_0$ and cover every plane. A minimizing through-cap must first minimize the own-fiber cap and thus have continuous normal along one of $(u_i,0)$. The strict paired assertion in that direction forces the base normal to vanish on every $z\in P$. Each such critical plane is proper in the middle fiber, so a parallel cap whose boundary does not pass through $Y$ and which contains $Y$ gains strictly positive middle volume.

The simplex vertex permutations act linearly on $x$ and preserve volume because they preserve $T_p$. Together with reflection in $t$, they preserve every fiber and the mixed measure. Their average on continuous vectors is zero: the simplex action has no fixed vector because a fixed point has equal barycentric coordinates and hence is the origin, while reflection handles $t$. The superlevel set of depth restricted to one fiber is convex. Indeed, a halfspace containing a convex combination of two points contains at least one of them. Taking the orbit average proves centroid maximality in each fiber.

For a nonzero base $z_0$, consider the cap through its centroid with margin $x_1+\alpha\cdot(z-z_0)$. At $\alpha=0$ its mass is $Q_0$. By the exact cap formula for small $\alpha$, the gradient is
$$
\frac{\delta Vd}{p}\sum_{z\in P}(r_z^0)^{d-1}(z-z_0)
=-\frac{\delta Vd}{p}z_0\sum_{z\in P}(r_z^0)^{d-1}.
$$
The negative-part correction has zero first derivative and the odd sum vanishes by symmetry. Moving $\alpha$ in the direction $z_0$ strictly decreases the mass, giving a strict gap at this and hence every point of the nonzero-base fiber.

At a middle point with $x\ne0$, some $u_i\cdot x>0$ because the normals span the equator and sum to zero. Shift the corresponding cylinder to this level, strictly losing volume in the middle fiber. At a point $(0,0,t_0)$ with $t_0\ne0$, use $x_1+v(t-t_0)\ge0$. At every slice of positive radius $\rho$ the threshold derivative of the canonical simplex cap at zero is $-\delta V_p\rho^{p-1}$, and the cap is globally threshold-Lipschitz with constant at most a dimension-only multiple of $\rho^{p-1}$ by its clipped power formula. The difference quotient in $v$ is dominated by this bound times $|t-t_0|$, integrable on each of the finitely many fibers. Differentiating under the integral, the odd $t$ term cancels and $\int_{-r}^r(r-|t|)^{p-1}dt=2r^p/p$. Thus the derivative of total cap mass is $-t_0(2\delta V_p/p)\sum_z(r_z^0)^p\ne0$. One sign of $v$ gives strict loss. This proves uniqueness at the baseline.

For two positive radial samples $(r_z),(s_z)$, nesting in each fiber bounds the difference of masses of any halfspace by $V\sum_z|r_z^d-s_z^d|$. This also bounds the difference of the depth infima at every fixed centroid. There are finitely many nonzero bases, each with strict baseline gap, so all those gaps persist for sufficiently close samples. The centroid argument applies to every radial sample, proving the claimed global maximizing mark.

statement:
Let $p\ge2$, $d=p+1$, and $T_p=\operatorname{conv}(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_p)$ with $v_0=(-1,\ldots,-1)$ and $v_i=v_0+(p+1)e_i$. Set $V_p=(p+1)^p/p!$, $\delta=(p/(p+1))^p$, and let
$$
K_p=\{(x,t): |t|\le1,\ x\in(1-|t|)T_p\},
\qquad V=2V_p/(p+1).
$$
Write $u_i=e_i$ for $1\le i\le p$ and $u_0=-\sum_{i=1}^p e_i$.

Let $B\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a compact convex body (a singleton for $n=0$), with $P=B\cap\mathbb Z^n$ centrally symmetric about and containing zero. Let $r^0:B\to(0,\infty)$ be continuous and concave with even sampled values. The actual body has fibers $r^0(z)K_p$ over $B$; mixed measure is summed $d$-volume at $P$. Put $M_0=V\sum_{z\in P}(r_z^0)^d$ and $Q_0=\delta M_0$.

The unique global maximizing point of raw mixed depth is $Y=(0,0,0)$, with depth $Q_0$. Its only critical cap traces on sampled planes are the canonical cylinders $u_i\cdot x\ge0$; an ambient representative of each has integer normal vanishing on $\operatorname{span}P$. Every fiber centroid is a within-fiber maximum. The central centroid remains a global maximizing point for all sufficiently nearby positive sampled radii realized by compatible radial families on the same base.
title: Actual radial bipyramid center, cap menu and persistent source gap
